subject: circuits

milestone.title: Kirchhoff's laws and nodal analysis
milestone.objective: Solve a circuit with two non-reference nodes using nodal analysis in under 10 minutes

sources.title: Course notes p.8 (fixture)
sources.text: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): the sum of the currents entering a node equals the sum of the currents leaving it. Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): the sum of the voltages around any closed loop is zero. Nodal analysis steps: 1. Choose a reference node (ground), usually the node with the most connections. 2. Label the voltage of every other node (V1, V2, ...) relative to the reference. 3. Write a KCL equation at each non-reference node, expressing each current with Ohm's law, for example (V1 - V2) / R. 4. Solve the equations for the node voltages. A circuit with n nodes gives n - 1 equations.

lesson_lines: - **Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL):** the currents entering a node add up to the currents leaving it.
- The voltages around any closed loop add up to zero.
1. Write a KCL equation at each non-reference node, writing each current with Ohm's law, e.g. (V1 − V2) / R.
2. Choose a reference node (ground): usually the node with the most connections.
3. Label the voltage of every other node (V1, V2, …) relative to ground.
4. Solve the equations for the node voltages.
A circuit with n nodes gives n − 1 equations.
Solve a circuit with two non-reference nodes (three nodes counting ground): find V1 and V2 with nodal analysis and check one KCL equation with your answers.
